name: Snap-on smile

lead: Snap-On Smile is a thin removable appliance that fits over the existing teeth to change how the smile looks. It is a branded dental product, and the term is also used loosely online for removable fake veneers.
The published literature is made up of dentists' case reports, mostly on older or medically complex patients, enamel disorders and implant provisionals.

paras: The appliance is a tooth-borne overdenture, reported to be made from acetal resin, that covers the teeth without altering them.
No trials have assessed it. Reports note the teeth can look too large in people with high smile lines or altered gums. It is described as temporary.

lead: Snap-On Smile is a removable cosmetic dental appliance made by the dental company DenMat. It is a thin tooth-borne overdenture that fits over a person's existing teeth, and is described in the dental literature as a temporary esthetic option rather than a permanent restoration [1][2]. In appearance culture, the term is also used generically for removable "fake veneers" that snap over the natural teeth.

Dentists have written about it mainly in case reports: for older patients with failing dentition and jaw disease, for people with the hereditary enamel disorder amelogenesis imperfecta, and as a provisional restoration during implant treatment [3][4][5][6]. These publications are clinician-authored case descriptions and do not include controlled trials.

paras: The appliance is described as a tooth-borne overdenture used for several temporary esthetic purposes [7]. One dental report describes a Snap-On Smile appliance fabricated from crystallized acetyl resin, and notes that the benefit can be limited in patients with a high smile line or altered gum architecture because the teeth can look too large; the author describes adding gum-colored silicone chairside to recreate gingival anatomy [7].

A 2013 article presented the appliance as a convenient solution for geriatric patients [3]. A 2016 report followed a 78-year-old man with osteonecrosis of the jaw and mandibular surgery, for whom most standard dental procedures were contraindicated, and described the appliance as restoring speech, chewing function and appearance over five years [1].

A 2015 paper discussed its use alongside facial esthetics for patients with amelogenesis imperfecta, a hereditary enamel disorder in which teeth can be discolored, sensitive and prone to decay, and in which patients often face psychosocial effects from appearance [2]. Other articles describe a quadrant version used as an implant temporary and further clinical applications [4][5][6][8].
No controlled trials were found. The published literature consists of clinician case reports and case series, including a five-year follow-up of a single patient [1][2][4][5][6][8].

Removable snap-on veneers are discussed in appearance communities as a non-invasive alternative to permanent veneers, which involve tooth preparation [9]. The dental literature on the branded product concerns medical and provisional uses rather than cosmetic purchases by people with healthy teeth.

timeline.event: Early clinical articles on Snap-on smile appear in Dentistry Today [8].
